payload.stem: Architect a scalable distributed subsystem optimizing Redis & Caching for a global enterprise platform at foundational difficulty.
payload.context: The service receives 80,000 requests per second. Highlight data flow, storage partitioning, and replication failover strategies.

criteria.name: Partitioning & Throughput
criteria.description: Detailed architectural breakdown of horizontal scaling and sharding.

model_answer: The design partitions traffic with consistent hashing rings, replicates asynchronously across availability zones, and enforces circuit breaking on slow upstream dependencies.
explanation: Under foundational conditions, scaling Redis & Caching requires decoupling synchronous database reads and utilizing bounded asynchronous event queues.

payload.stem: What are the primary operational bottlenecks when monitoring and tuning Redis & Caching in production environments?

criteria.name: Bottleneck Identification
criteria.description: Pinpoints concrete failure triggers (I/O, locks, CPU, network).

model_answer: The primary bottleneck is disk I/O saturation and thread pool exhaustion during burst traffic. Mitigation relies on request coalescing and adaptive rate limiting.
explanation: When requests surge, unbuffered downstream queries saturate connection pools, creating cascading latency across the entire microservice ecosystem.
